name: Tharnariun's Hope
summary: In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender seeks a cure for the sick thistle bears. His trap calms them long enough to bring them to his camp.

sections.title: A Gentle Snare
sections.body: Tharnariun Treetender made a trap to calm the sick thistle bears. A mysterious affliction has made them more and more frenzied and violent across Darkshore. He hopes to cure them instead of seeing them killed. Set on the ground, Tharnariun's Hope shines with a soothing light. A rabid thistle bear that crosses it grows calm for a time and can follow a traveler back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

sections.title: The Elusive Remedy
sections.body: Tharnariun Treetender's healing magic cannot save a captured bear. The trap quiets the maddened animal without harming it, but the corruption is more vicious than he expected. When he directs his healing into the bear, his magic clashes with the infection. The animal collapses and dies. Though his first attempt ends in heartbreak, Tharnariun remains determined to learn the true nature of the forest's sickness.

faq.answer: Tharnariun's Hope calms a rabid thistle bear for a time. Set on the forest floor, it casts a field of light that lets a traveler lead the bear peacefully back to Tharnariun Treetender.

faq.q: Why does Tharnariun want a live bear captured?
faq.answer: Tharnariun believes the sickness afflicting Darkshore's wildlife can be cured instead of answered with slaughter. He needs a living bear to test his cleansing remedies.

faq.q: Can you get another trap if you lose it?
faq.answer: Yes. Tharnariun says his hope is eternal. If the trap is triggered in vain or lost in the wild, return to him for another.

faq.q: What happens to the bear once it is brought back?
faq.answer: When the bear reaches Tharnariun, he casts healing magic to purge the corruption. The sickness overwhelms the beast, and it dies within moments.

angles.text: As a druid, you can see Tharnariun's trap as a choice to preserve corrupted beasts while there is still a chance to redeem them.
As a night elf, you know the thistle bears are beloved in Darkshore. Their sickness makes Tharnariun's trap a sign of desperate compassion.
